- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overcorrects downward — raise forecast modestly to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates upward price spikes in the next 5–10 days after strong positive sentiment — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.  
- Model often overestimates downward moves after negative sentiment — reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent range to avoid premature bearish reversal.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 3–5% below recent 10-day average, adjust upward; if 3–5% above, adjust downward — especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed.  
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag by 1–2 days in capturing sentiment-driven momentum — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending.  
- Overshoot after spikes: if model forecasts a sharp spike followed by a drop, reduce the peak by 1–3% to avoid overestimating volatility.  
- Sentiment reversal: if sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast 1–2% per day of lag.
